concurrency_primitives: goroutines, buffered channels, sync.WaitGroup; one goroutine per dataset streams and aggregates its CSV (main.go:211-232); bounded worker pool (<=8) with local maps re-aggregates pre-aggregated neighborhood|month counts (analysis.go:29-148)
design_patterns: None named or realized; procedural split into ingest (main.go), aggregation + report functions (analysis.go), date parsing (dates.go)
questions: Which neighborhoods have the highest combined volume of 311 requests and crime records?
What is the Pearson correlation between neighborhood-level 311 counts and crime counts?
Which neighborhoods are above average in both datasets?
What 311 request types are most common in those high-activity neighborhoods?
How do monthly 311 and crime counts change Jan-Sep 2026?
overview: Small single-package Go program in three files: two goroutines stream the two CSVs into count maps, a bounded worker pool merges pre-aggregated neighborhood-month counts, and five report functions print tables and ASCII bars. Readable and deterministic, with honest caveats printed, but dataset logic is dispatched on display-name strings, keys are 'a|b' strings, no design pattern is realized and there is one small test.
stakeholder_value: The reports show that large neighborhoods have more 311 requests and more crime (r=0.777) and list the top ones, which is coincidental counting rather than insight; nothing is normalized for size. No stakeholders are named, and the headline 311 category is a city-run proactive rat sweep misread as resident demand, so a Mayor's Office or DPW would learn little that is actionable.
issues: No stakeholders named; questions are generic count rankings and a size-driven correlation.
Report 4 headline 'SW-RAT RUBOUT PROACTIVE' is a city-initiated program, not resident demand.
Worker pool only re-aggregates ~15k pre-aggregated keys; CSV parsing is sequential per file.
Prebuilt binaries shipped without execute permission (mode 0666) and an executable copy was SIGKILLed by macOS; could not be verified (source build graded).
go.mod go 1.27.2 forces a toolchain download on older Go installs.
rationale: Clean build, two bundled real datasets and a successful end-to-end run earn full marks on build, real_data and runs_results. Points are lost for partial concurrency (no parallel parsing; pool does trivial work), basic undocumented memory handling, a small single-package design without a realized pattern, and shallow count-based questions with no named stakeholders. 71/100, C.
